chapter_title: The Three Earths that Exist, they bear Fruit.
spiritual_reading:
There are three distinct degrees within the whole of life that are being brought into order by continual operation. In the beginning each degree resists and is unyielding to the formative work flowing into it; afterward, when it has been opened and made receptive, it produces genuine effects for those who perform uses within it.

One degree is the outermost plane in which people actually live and act. Into this plane higher things are introduced and fixed by means of firm truths that can work upon stubborn states; by these, what is confused is arranged into an ordered pattern, what is compacted is opened, and what is merely surface is made capable of receiving inward influence. When this has been done, the same outer plane yields actual goods of life as outcomes from the order impressed upon it.

The second degree is the living interior of a person, the holy receiving faculty itself. It is present through the whole range of the person, within and without, in what is higher and what is lower, because it is the common subject into which life can flow. The agents that work upon it are the two universal powers of heaven that give understanding and love; they continually move through all spiritual states and operate unceasingly, so that this interior may be drawn away from what is merely self and turned toward their own quality. When it is thus acted upon, it is raised into higher state, it withdraws from every lower confinement in which it had been held, and it becomes an added strength and enrichment to all the lower forms that depend upon it.

fills.notes: The three ‘earths’ are discrete degrees. In the beginning each degree is unreceptive and opposes formative influx; thus the soil ‘resists’ the farmer’s work before it is opened.

Change from editor’s ‘good’. In the oldest cosmological register the first yield of an opened degree is not moral goodness but the right product of order, i.e., what is genuine and according to form. Correspondentially, after resistance ceases it bears ‘true fruit’ for the operators of use.

The outer earth is worked by hard implements (iron hoes): this corresponds to firm truths acting on stubborn natural states. The missing participle should name the heavy breaking-up action preceding cultivation.

Change from editor’s ‘making’. The sequence names distinct operations: striking with iron, then forming the furrows. ‘Cutting the furrows’ matches the correspondential idea of truth dividing and arranging the compacted natural plane into order.

fills.fill: in order. Afterwards they harvest fruit from it
fills.notes: The gap completes the cultivation sequence with an ordering result, then resumes the stated outcome (harvest). Correspondentially, once the outer plane is arranged into order it can yield effects (‘fruit’) from that impressed order.

assessment: Most gaps are tightly constrained by the three-degree schema: initial resistance, then receptivity and yield; and the natural-field operations corresponding to the ordering action of firm truths. Exact verbal choices in ¶2 #3 remain the least constrained, but the required sense is clear: the work results in an ordered state, then fruit is gathered.
